_README: MARKER-ONLY. Never fetched by the student's browser until a teacher/marker PDF is generated. Never render any of this on the student-facing page. See CLAUDE.md §5's assessment-security amendment.

markingScheme.criterion: Quotes the Spanish words of one real task from their own Record (e.g. 'aquellas gafas', 'nos ponemos') that they got wrong or needed two tries for.
markingScheme.accept: Any task that appears in the student's own Record with Tries 2 or Right = No; if the student had a perfect Record, any task from the Record. Accents not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: Describing a rule in general with no task or Spanish words taken from their Record.

markingScheme.criterion: States the correct rule behind that task in English (e.g. demonstrative matches distance AND the noun's gender/number; reflexive pronoun and verb ending match the person; colour adjective agrees with the noun and comes after it).
markingScheme.accept: Any correct rule that fits the quoted task, in the student's own words.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying 'I got it wrong' or 'it changes' with no stated reason or pattern.

markingScheme.criterion: Writes one new, correct Spanish example that follows the stated rule.
markingScheme.accept: Any grammatically correct Unit 7 example (minor accent slips allowed if the form is clear), different from the quoted task.
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeating the quoted task, or a new example with an incorrect ending/verb form.

markingScheme.criterion: Sentence 1 uses llevar correctly (llevo/lleva/llevas/llevamos/llevan to match the subject) with TWO clothing items, each with a suitable article (un/una/unos/unas or el/la/los/las).
markingScheme.accept: Any correct form of llevar matching the subject and two Unit 7 items with correct article gender/number. Minor accent slips are allowed.
markingScheme.insufficient: Only one item, a wrong verb form for the subject, or articles with the wrong gender (e.g. 'un falda').

markingScheme.criterion: Colours are placed AFTER the noun and agree with it (una camiseta blanca; unos zapatos negros).
markingScheme.accept: At least two colour adjectives, both after their noun and agreeing in gender/number (invariable azul/verde are fine).
markingScheme.insufficient: Colours placed before the noun, or not agreeing (una camiseta blanco).

markingScheme.criterion: Sentence 2 uses ponerse correctly (me pongo / se pone etc.) AND sentence 3 asks the price with the correct far-distance demonstrative for a jacket: '¿Cuánto cuesta aquella chaqueta?' (or equivalent).
markingScheme.accept: Both parts present and correct. Award the mark only if BOTH the ponerse sentence and the price question with aquella are correct.
markingScheme.insufficient: Only one of the two correct; or 'aquel chaqueta' / 'esta chaqueta' for a far-away jacket.

criteria.source: = the Explain question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: None of the three analytic points achieved: no real task quoted from the Record, no correct rule, and no correct new example.
Achieves only ONE of the three: quotes a real task from their Record OR states a correct rule OR gives a correct new example — the other two are missing or incorrect.
Achieves TWO of the three: e.g. quotes a real task and states the correct rule, but the new example is missing or incorrect.
Quotes a real task from their own Record, states the correct rule in English, and gives a correct new Spanish example — all three analytic points present.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: None of the three analytic points achieved: llevar sentence, colour placement/agreement, and ponerse + price question are all missing or incorrect.
Achieves only ONE of the three analytic points (correct llevar sentence with two items; colours after the noun and agreeing; correct ponerse sentence AND price question with aquella).
Achieves TWO of the three analytic points.
Correct llevar sentence with two items and articles, colours after the noun and agreeing, and a correct ponerse sentence plus price question with aquella — all three analytic points present.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across BOTH the Explain and Apply answers together — independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks in use_of_evidence and spanish_use above.

levels.descriptor: Too unclear or incomplete for the meaning to be followed reliably.
Main meaning understandable, but organisation, vocabulary or precision cause some difficulty.
Clear and logical, uses Unit 7 vocabulary, and is easy to follow. Minor spelling or accent slips that do not harm meaning are not penalised.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply). Award marks point-by-point using each question's markingScheme: each point is worth the marks stated, is independent unless it names a dependsOn point (award it only if that earlier point was also awarded), and each point's 'accept'/'insufficient' tell you what does and doesn't count. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain markingScheme's 3 points, and spanish_use's 3 marks ARE the Apply markingScheme's 3 points — the rubric levels restate the same points as bands; award each set once, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy. Use the student's logged Record (nivel/tarea/respuesta/correcto/intentos in simulation_results.trials) to verify any task they claim to quote. Students are beginners (A1): accept valid alternative wording; do not penalise a missing accent unless it changes the meaning. Total is out of 15 (7 auto + 3 + 3 + 2). Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 80 words.
